articles.title: Sewer lid closes, Ahmedabad family's hopes drown: No body, no accidental death case in Manisha Salat tragedy
articles.summary: Ahmedabad: Search ends for 10-year-old Manisha Salat missing after falling into an open sewer; no body found, so police haven’t filed an accidental death case.
articles.body: AHMEDABAD: The sewer on Narol-Vishala road, which swallowed a 10-year-old, now has a lid.The search for Manisha Salat’s body has been called off, and the investigation into her disappearance has receded from public attention. But for her family, the tragedy has not ended.Her parents, Paru and Bala Salat, and their four other children live next to a footpath in Ganeshnagar, struggling for food and shelter. Three of the four remaining children are visually impaired.Ajay, 13, is the only one who can see, and Maya, 11, Mangal, 7, and Arman, 4, can’t. Paru said she had taken Manisha to several doctors and was hoping to take her to an eye hospital near Civil Hospital, but tragedy struck.“When Manisha fell into that gutter, she cried, ‘Mummy, I have fallen!’ That was the last time I heard her voice. I turned around and she was gone,” Paru said, recalling the afternoon. The family had just got off an autorickshaw and was heading home.The open manhole was concealed by overgrown grass. Paru said she too slipped near it and Manisha, walking behind her, lost her footing and fell backwards into the deep drainage shaft.“I searched through the grass with my feet, and my leg sank into the opening. That was when I realised there was a deep pit. I wanted to jump in after her, but my husband stopped me and asked people to help,” she said.The incident occurred around 3pm, but emergency personnel arrived only around 5pm, she alleged. The family remained at the spot for 10 days, hoping for some trace of Manisha. Nothing identifiable was recovered. “Not even her clothes were found,” said Paru.No accidental death has so far been reported due to want of a body.“The rescuers were late by two to three hours. By then, my daughter’s body had dissolved in that chemical-filled water. We searched for days, but did not get even her clothes or bones,” Paru said.Her anger is now directed at AMC. “They could not ensure that my daughter was safe, but were very quick to take away our belongings. When they demolish our shelters, they take everything, including our bedding and identity papers. I had to pay Rs 3,000 to get our Aadhaar card and documents back,” she alleged.The family lives on casual labour and by hawking toys. Bala also performs magic tricks on the streets at night. “Sometimes, we can scrape together just one meal in two or three days. There is no place for us to bathe,” Paru said.Paru said the family had lived in the Pirana-Piplaj road area for nearly 15 years, moving between makeshift settlements after repeated evictions. Neighbours from Bharwad and Muslim communities now provide drinking water from their taps, she said.“We had hoped our children would get treatment and have a better life. articles.title: ‘Why make us suffer?’: Devotees wait for hours as DK Shivakumar offers prayers; slippers hurled at TV screen
articles.summary: Devotees at Hasanamba temple were stopped during CM DK Shivakumar’s visit, sparking protests; some threw slippers at a TV showing his sanctum visuals.
articles.body: HASSAN: An unusual incident occurred when chief minister DK Shivakumar visited the Hasanamba temple along with his wife on Sunday afternoon.At around 12 noon, the chief minister entered the sanctum sanctorum and performed special prayers for some time. Meanwhile, the entry of devotees through the general darshan queue was temporarily stopped until the CM completed his visit.Thousands of devotees, particularly women, who had already been waiting in long queues for several hours, became furious over the delay.Their anger intensified when visuals of the chief minister sitting inside the sanctum were telecast on a television screen installed near the queue. Watching the visuals, several women openly criticised the CM, questioning why devotees were being made to suffer.“People elect a chief minister to protect their interests, not to cause them hardship,” one woman reportedly remarked. Several other devotees in the queue supported her criticism.In a fit of anger, some devotees even removed their slippers and threw them at the television screen displaying the chief minister’s visuals. articles.title: Off-grid hut owner wins battle to keep living in home near Crymych
articles.summary: The man has lived in the self-built hut since 2020 - but never told authorities or asked for permission.
articles.body:
An off-grid hut that produces its own heating and electricity can continue to be the home of the man who built it, a council has decided.

Geoffrey Finnimore, a self-employed architectural designer, erected the structure in Glandwr, near Crymych, in 2020, but never told authorities or asked for permission.

Pembrokeshire council told him he must apply for retrospective permission for the home that is self-sufficient, and also collects rain water.

However, the local authority found that because it has now been occupied as a home for more than four years, it is immune from prosecution action.

"Without my home, which I created to solve my own problems without state assistance, having to pay for other accommodation would be catastrophic for my finances and well-being," Finnimore said.

The council asked him to apply for a lawful development certificate for the property.

This is a formal legal document confirming the development is lawful.

But as he had lived there for more than four years, it meant he could not be prosecuted, so his application was accepted, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said.

Finnimore has been the principal custodian of 4.5 acres of land at Coed Troednoeth, Tir y Gafel since the previous owner left in 2018.

They had lived at the site in a campervan with a lean-to structure, according to the council.

But Finnimore described this as "less than adequate" for his health and well-being, so started developing the hut.

In a personal statement to the local authority, he confirmed he had lived at the site for more than 10 years, earns less than £10,000 a year as a self-employed worker, and provided evidence of his long-term residency.

He added: "This application has been sought by the council, and I have had to comply out of a position of vulnerability with respect to the prospect of enforcement against a building and living situation that has been demonstrated to be well-established and that I hold is deemed lawful."

"In the context of a housing and a cost-of-living crisis I have taken care of my own needs.

"So far as the council's responsibilities in that context goes, I see that as one less problem to solve.

"Conversely, I would consider a rejection of a well-justified application like this as a contribution that exacerbates these deep and present social concerns."

Council officers granted the certificate because they found, on the balance of probabilities, that Coed Troednoeth had existed and been occupied as a home for more than four years before the application, making it immune from enforcement action.

It added: "In June 2020, the land was purchased by Mr Finnimore and in November 2020, he began using the building as his principal dwelling, hence the justification to apply for a certificate of lawful use."

articles.summary: O g1 compila concursos, processos seletivos e vagas de empregos com inscrições em andamento, contemplando diferentes áreas e níveis de escolaridade.
articles.body:
Oportunidades de emprego e de ingresso no serviço público estão abertas no Ceará, com vagas em Fortaleza e em outros municípios, nesta segunda-feira (9).

O g1 compila concursos, processos seletivos, cursos e vagas de empregos com inscrições em andamento, contemplando diferentes áreas e níveis de escolaridade.

Veja oportunidades disponíveis no Ceará. — Foto: Reprodução Freepik

Confira abaixo as oportunidades desta semana:

A Prefeitura Municipal de Boa Viagem está com vagas abertas para um concurso público para cargos efetivos e formação de cadastro de reserva. Organizado pela Fundação Cetrede, o certame contempla oportunidades para profissionais de níveis fundamental incompleto, fundamental completo, médio e superior.

No total, o edital disponibiliza 1.001 vagas de início imediato e 2.002 vagas para formação de cadastro de reserva, totalizando 3.003 oportunidades

As inscrições serão efetuadas exclusivamente no site da Fundação Cetrede até 7 de dezembro de 2026.

O Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) oferta 1.527 vagas temporárias de recenseador no Ceará, para atuação no 12º Censo Agropecuário, Florestal e Aquícola.

Os interessados podem se inscrever até as 23h59 do dia 25 de novembro de 2026 , no site da Fundação Cesgranrio , com o pagamento da taxa de R$ 70.

Segundo o IBGE, os recenseadores receberão salário mensal de R$ 1.741, além de pagamento por produtividade. Também estão previstos benefícios como auxílio-alimentação de R$ 1.192, auxílio pré-escolar, 13º salário proporcional, férias proporcionais acrescidas de um terço constitucional e auxílio para custeio dos deslocamentos.

A CR Duarte Engenharia está com 63 oportunidades de emprego em Fortaleza e Região Metropolitana na área da construção civil. A empresa busca novas contratações para as atividades de 2027, ano em que prevê iniciar sete novas obras.

Os cargos disponíveis abrangem diferentes áreas e níveis de formação, nas áreas técnica, administrativa e operacional.

Os interessados devem realizar a candidatura de forma online, até janeiro de 2027, por meio de formulário eletrônico ( acesse aqui ). Os candidatos deverão preencher os dados de contato e enviar o currículo pela plataforma.

A Lojas Americanas está contratando 114 profissionais temporários no Ceará para reforçar suas operações de lojas visando a Black Friday 2026 (no fim do mês de novembro). Há vagas em Fortaleza, Caucaia, Juazeiro do Norte, Maracanaú, Sobral, Crato, Itapipoca e Eusébio.

Não é necessária experiência prévia para concorrer às vagas: os requisitos são idade mínima de 18 anos e ensino médio completo. O estabelecimento se prepara para receber o maior fluxo de consumidores do período.

As inscrições podem ser feitas até hoje, 9 de novembro no Portal de Carreiras Americanas .

A Prefeitura de Fortaleza, em parceria com o CIEE, continua com inscrições abertas para o Programa de Jovens Talentos 2026 , que oferece vagas de estágio para estudantes do ensino médio, técnico e superior na administração pública municipal. As inscrições são gratuitas, seguem abertas até 31 de dezembro de 2026 e devem ser feitas exclusivamente pelo portal do CIEE .

Os estagiários recebem bolsa-auxílio de R$ 750 (ensino superior), R$ 550 (técnico) e R$ 450 (ensino médio), além de auxílio-transporte. A carga horária é de 4 horas diárias. Para participar, é preciso ter pelo menos 16 anos e estar regularmente matriculado em instituição reconhecida pelo MEC.

O Sine Municipal de Fortaleza está com 2.816 vagas de emprego abertas nesta semana. As oportunidades contemplam 208 profissões e são ofertadas por 283 empresas parceiras de diferentes setores da economia.

articles.title: 2026 deve ficar entre os 4 anos mais quentes já registrados, diz ONU | G1
articles.standfirst: Temperatura global ficou 1,47°C acima do nível pré-industrial entre janeiro e setembro.
articles.summary: Temperatura global ficou 1,47°C acima do nível pré-industrial entre janeiro e setembro.
articles.body:
Pedestre se protege do calor na região central da cidade de São Paulo. — Foto: BRUNO ESCOLASTICO/E.FOTOGRAFIA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

O ano de 2026 deve terminar entre os quatro mais quentes já registrados no planeta, segundo um novo relatório da Organização Meteorológica Mundial (OMM) , organismo da ONU responsável por acompanhar o clima, o tempo e os recursos hídricos no mundo.

Entre janeiro e setembro, a temperatura média global ficou cerca de 1,47°C acima do nível pré-industrial , usado como referência para medir o avanço do aquecimento global.

O valor está próximo das médias registradas em 2023 e 2025, mas ainda abaixo do recorde de 2024, quando o planeta terminou o ano 1,55°C mais quente que no período anterior à industrialização.

Segundo a OMM, 2023, 2024, 2025 e 2026 formam agora o grupo dos quatro anos mais quentes já registrados.

E a temperatura média deste ano ainda pode subir até dezembro .

Isso porque o El Niño, fenômeno natural caracterizado pelo aquecimento anormal das águas do Oceano Pacífico Equatorial, vem ganhando força desde agosto e deve continuar pelo menos até o início de 2027.

A OMM afirma que o atual episódio pode se tornar o El Niño mais forte já registrado até dezembro.

🌡️ ENTENDA: o El Niño não cria sozinho o aquecimento global. Ele libera para a atmosfera parte do calor armazenado nos oceanos. Como o planeta já está mais quente por causa das emissões de gases de efeito estufa, o fenômeno pode elevar temporariamente ainda mais a temperatura global.

Em geral, o El Niño acrescenta cerca de 0,1°C a 0,2°C à temperatura média do planeta, segundo a OMM.

Seu maior efeito costuma aparecer no ano seguinte ao início do fenômeno, o que aumenta a preocupação também com 2027.

“O El Niño não adiciona calor novo ao planeta. Ele libera calor do oceano, que está mais quente do que em qualquer outro momento já medido. Há simplesmente mais calor disponível para ser liberado”, afirma Celeste Saulo, secretária-geral da OMM.

O relatório mostra que esse excesso de calor também aparece nos oceanos, no gelo e no nível do mar.

O nível médio dos oceanos atingiu um novo recorde em 2026, e a quantidade de calor armazenada nos mares continua aumentando. Cerca de 90% do excesso de calor acumulado pelo planeta é absorvido pelos oceanos.

A quantidade de energia acumulada no sistema climático também chegou aos maiores níveis desde o início das medições.

Isso ocorre porque os gases de efeito estufa fazem com que o planeta retenha mais energia do que consegue devolver ao espaço .

As geleiras também seguem perdendo massa. Em 2025, desapareceram mais de 400 bilhões de toneladas de gelo, quantidade que, segundo a OMM, seria suficiente para encher cinco piscinas olímpicas por segundo durante todo o ano.

Ao mesmo tempo, a quantidade de água armazenada nos continentes — em rios , reservatórios , solos , aquíferos , neve e geleiras — vem diminuindo globalmente desde 2014.

Em 2025, 42% da área analisada do planeta apresentou reservas de água abaixo do normal.

A ONU também chama atenção para os impactos já sentidos pela população.

Ondas de calor, secas e incêndios na Europa provocaram mais de 30 mil mortes em excesso , segundo estimativas preliminares citadas no relatório. Na Índia, cerca de 146,5 milhões de pessoas foram expostas ao calor extremo durante uma onda de calor em abril.

A expectativa é que o El Niño amplifique parte desses riscos nos próximos meses, atuando como um fator adicional para ondas de calor, secas, chuvas intensas e ciclones tropicais em diferentes partes do mundo.

O relatório divulgado agora reúne dados disponíveis até setembro. A versão final sobre o clima global em 2026 será publicada pela OMM em março de 2027.

articles.title: Redação do Enem 2026: que repertórios cabiam no tema? Veja exemplos | G1
articles.standfirst: Constituição de 1988, Reforma Sanitária e pandemia de Covid-19 são exemplos de referências que poderiam ser usadas na redação sobre o SUS, desde que relacionadas aos argumentos.
articles.summary: Constituição de 1988, Reforma Sanitária e pandemia de Covid-19 são exemplos de referências que poderiam ser usadas na redação sobre o SUS, desde que relacionadas aos argumentos.
articles.body:
Provas do 1º dia do Enem 2026 — Foto: Bruna Araújo/MEC

A Constituição Federal de 1988, a história da criação do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) e a pandemia de Covid-19 são alguns exemplos de repertório sociocultural que poderiam ser utilizados pelos candidatos na redação do Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) 2026 , aplicada no último domingo (8).

O tema escolhido foi “ A valorização do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) como direito universal ”.

Segundo professores de redação ouvidos pelo g1 , o desafio era relacionar referências históricas, sociais e culturais à importância do sistema público de saúde e aos obstáculos que ainda dificultam sua valorização.

Uma das referências mais diretamente relacionadas ao assunto é a Constituição de 1988 , que estabeleceu a saúde como um direito de todos e um dever do Estado.

O artigo 196, inclusive, apareceu entre os textos motivadores apresentados aos estudantes.

A legislação poderia ser utilizada para discutir a distância entre o direito garantido pela Constituição e as dificuldades enfrentadas por parte da população para acessar os serviços de saúde.

No entanto, apenas reproduzir o conteúdo da coletânea não seria suficiente para demonstrar domínio de repertório sociocultural.

Outro caminho possível seria abordar a história da Reforma Sanitária brasileira , movimento que ajudou a estabelecer as bases para a criação do SUS.

A referência permitiria mostrar como o acesso à saúde deixou de estar associado principalmente à contribuição previdenciária e passou a ser reconhecido como um direito de todos os brasileiros.

A pandemia de Covid-19 também poderia servir de repertório. Nesse caso, os candidatos poderiam destacar a atuação do SUS na vacinação e no enfrentamento da emergência sanitária, relacionando esses serviços à importância de fortalecer a estrutura pública de saúde.

Para Daniela Toffoli, professora de Redação do Curso Anglo, da Cogna Educação, havia dois caminhos principais para desenvolver a argumentação: a falta de financiamento adequado do sistema e o desconhecimento de parte da população sobre os serviços oferecidos pelo SUS (VEJA OS VÍDEOS ABAIXO).

Segundo ela, a palavra “ valorização ”, presente no enunciado, já indicava que os estudantes precisavam identificar um problema.

Assim, seria possível discutir tanto as limitações de recursos quanto a falta de informação e o estigma associado ao atendimento público.

O cuidado, porém, era não transformar a redação em uma simples lista de problemas da saúde pública.

A professora ressalta que o candidato também precisava abordar o caráter universal do SUS, relacionando os argumentos à garantia do acesso à saúde para toda a população.

Embora referências como a Constituição e a pandemia tenham relação direta com o tema, os professores ressaltam que não basta mencionar acontecimentos históricos, leis ou conceitos conhecidos para garantir uma boa avaliação.

O repertório sociocultural é considerado na Competência 2 da redação , que avalia, entre outros aspectos, a capacidade de mobilizar conhecimentos de diferentes áreas para desenvolver o tema proposto.

Na cartilha de 2026, o Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Ine p) voltou a alertar para os chamados “ repertórios de bolso ”: referências memorizadas e utilizadas de maneira genérica, sem uma conexão efetiva com o assunto discutido.

Para ser bem utilizado, o repertório sociocultural precisa estar integrado à argumentação .

Não basta citar uma lei, um acontecimento histórico, um livro ou uma frase conhecida: é necessário explicar como essa referência se relaciona com o tema e contribui para defender o ponto de vista apresentado.

Na prática, alguns cuidados ajudam a tornar o repertório mais relevante para a redação:

📚 Apresentar a referência : identificar corretamente a lei, o acontecimento histórico, a obra ou o conceito utilizado. No caso do SUS, por exemplo, seria possível mencionar a Constituição Federal de 1988, que reconheceu a saúde como um direito de todos.

🔎 Explicar seu significado : contextualizar a informação, demonstrando que o candidato compreende sua importância. Ao citar a Constituição, por exemplo, seria necessário explicar o que significa garantir o acesso universal à saúde.

🔗 Relacionar ao argumento : mostrar como a referência ajuda a sustentar a ideia defendida. O estudante poderia discutir, por exemplo, a distância entre o direito previsto na Constituição e as dificuldades enfrentadas pela população para acessar determinados serviços.

💡 Desenvolver uma análise própria : utilizar a referência como ponto de partida para uma reflexão, e não apenas como uma informação isolada. A pandemia de Covid-19, por exemplo, poderia servir para discutir a importância da estrutura pública de saúde e da vacinação.

⚠️ Evitar citações genéricas ou forçadas : mencionar uma obra ou um pensador famoso apenas para demonstrar conhecimento não garante uma boa argumentação. A referência precisa ter uma relação clara com o assunto e acrescentar algo à discussão.

articles.summary: A UFU está entre as melhores universidades do Brasil, ocupando o 18º lugar no RUF e alcançando o topo nacional em inovação e cursos de Engenharia e Odontologia.
articles.body:
Fachada da Universidade Federal de Uberlândia — Foto: Reprodução/TV Integração

A Universidade Federal de Uberlândia ( UFU ) está entre as vinte melhores universidades do Brasil em 2026, de acordo com dados divulgados pelo Ranking Universitário da Folha.

Em 2025, a UFU ocupava a 16ª posição e passou para a 18ª neste ano, uma queda de duas colocações. Ao todo, 205 universidades brasileiras foram avaliadas. Com isso, a universidade retorna ao lugar que ocupava em 2023. Essa é a segunda queda consecutiva no ranking, já que de 2024 para 2025 a instituição caiu do 14º para o 16º lugar.

O ranking é liderado pela Universidade de São Paulo (USP), Universidade Estadual de Campinas (Unicamp) e Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG).

O levantamento considerou cinco categorias: pesquisa, ensino, mercado de trabalho, inovação e internacionalização.

A universidade se destacou em 8º lugar em inovação no Brasil e em 2º lugar em Minas Gerais. Segundo a diretora de Inovação e Transferência de Tecnologia da UFU, Luciana Carvalho, o resultado mostra uma ciência de alta qualidade e que está cada vez mais conectada com os desafios reais.

"O principal papel da inovação dentro da universidade é fazer o conhecimento produzido aqui dentro gerar impacto lá fora. A universidade pesquisa, ensina e forma pessoas, e a inovação é a ponte que leva tudo isso para a vida das pessoas, seja em um novo produto, um tratamento, uma tecnologia para o campo ou uma empresa que nasce de uma pesquisa. Inovar também é uma forma de valorizar o pesquisador: é mostrar que o trabalho dele, muitas vezes de anos, pode mudar realidades", disse.

Ainda segundo Luciana, a UFU tem diferentes caminhos para deixar as soluções criadas pelos pesquisadores mais práticas.

"Acompanhamos o pesquisador em todo o caminho. Pela Agência Intelecto, nosso Núcleo de Inovação Tecnológica, cuidamos da proteção da propriedade intelectual, como patentes, registros de software e marcas, e da transferência dessas tecnologias para empresas por meio de licenciamentos e parcerias. Contamos também com o CIAEM (Centro de Incubação de Atividades Empreendedoras), nossa incubadora, e com o TecnoUFU, o parque tecnológico, que apoiam o nascimento e o crescimento de empresas de base tecnológica. Temos o CIEU, o Centro de Inovação e Empreendedorismo Universitário, que é um espaço de encontro entre a universidade e o setor produtivo. Lá, estudantes, pesquisadores e empresas se aproximam, trocam experiências e constroem soluções juntos", completou.

O levantamento considera informações de universidades em funcionamento no Brasil e utiliza indicadores nacionais e internacionais. A avaliação considera os 42 cursos universitários com o maior número de ingressantes no país. Na UFU, 39 dos atuais 93 foram avaliados. Cada carreira considera uma série de graduações da mesma área que têm diferentes nomenclaturas. Na UFU, por exemplo, o curso de Jornalismo foi incluído na nomenclatura "Comunicação".

articles.title: Promessas para aumentar a imunidade podem fazer mais mal do que bem, alertam pesquisadores | G1
articles.standfirst: Manter o sistema imune significa manter o organismo em equilíbrio, e não potencializar excessivamente suas funções e capacidades.
articles.summary: Manter o sistema imune significa manter o organismo em equilíbrio, e não potencializar excessivamente suas funções e capacidades.
articles.body:
Promessas para aumentar a imunidade podem fazer mais mal do que bem, alertam pesquisadores — Foto: Adobe Stock

Todos nós queremos um sistema imune que funcione bem para nos ajudar a combater bactérias e vírus invasores e nos recuperarmos mais rapidamente de doenças. Mas recomendações populares sobre como “fortalecer o sistema imune” podem ser mais um obstáculo do que uma ajuda.

Promover o fortalecimento do sistema imune é uma tendência na internet. Criadores de conteúdo compartilham receitas para fortalecer o sistema imune — desde bebidas até sopas até tijelas de poke e pães de abóbora. Livros sobre nutrição falam de “imunidade superpotente”, enquanto clínicas naturopáticas compartilham “dicas” para fortalecer o sistema imune.

A expressão “fortalecer” tornou-se tão comum que aparece com frequência em conteúdos sobre saúde de instituições acadêmicas conceituadas.

A pandemia da COVID-19 — mais do que nunca na memória recente — fez com que o público refletisse profundamente sobre a imunidade. Como pesquisadores interdisciplinares de saúde pública que estudam as forças influentes que moldam as percepções do público, o aumento do discurso sobre o reforço imune durante esse período chamou nossa atenção. Pesquisamos esse conceito em alta nos resultados de busca do Google e em redes sociais como o Instagram.

Constatamos que isso é problemático de duas maneiras: em primeiro lugar, o conteúdo frequentemente apresenta imprecisões científicas sobre o funcionamento do sistema imune. Em segundo lugar, dá destaque a empresas que promovem produtos ou serviços ineficazes. Em um momento em que a confiança em intervenções baseadas em evidências, como vacinas, está abalada, isso pode levar a resultados negativos para nossa saúde.

Nem todo conteúdo sobre o fortalecimento da imunidade é impreciso ou prejudicial. Informações provenientes de pesquisas ou de organizações médicas geralmente se concentram na alimentação saudável, prática de exercícios, sono adequado e na prevenção dos malefícios do tabaco e do álcool. A ideia de “potencilizar” ou “aumentar” a imunidade, no entanto, continua sendo fundamentalmente equivocada. O sistema imune precisa ser mantido, não potenciado.

Isso porque o sistema imune de cada pessoa é complexo, composto por células, tecidos, órgãos e proteínas . Esse sistema atua de forma inata e não específica para manter afastados germes invasores nocivos, utilizando, por exemplo, a pele e as membranas mucosas como barreira protetora. E ele também atua de forma adaptativa, mobilizando uma resposta direcionada e específica contra invasores nocivos.

O sistema imune adaptativo utiliza células B que produzem anticorpos — proteínas especiais que se ligam aos germes invasores e os marcam para destruição ou neutralizam seus efeitos. Existem também células T, que atuam como destruidoras, caçando e matando células que foram infectadas por germes.

Surpreendentemente, o processo adaptativo do sistema imune cria células de memória dos patógenos contra os quais luta. Quando o mesmo invasor volta a entrar no corpo, ele pode ser rapidamente reconhecido e combatido de forma mais eficaz. Um sistema imune que funciona bem também diferencia corretamente entre as células do próprio organismo e as células invasoras.

Um sistema imune com desempenho insuficiente aumenta a possibilidade e a gravidade de infecções. Mas um sistema imune hiperativo pode levar a uma série de doenças autoimunes, como a artrite reumatoide e a esclerose múltipla. Manter o sistema imune, portanto, envolve equilíbrio — e não sobrecarregar suas funções e capacidades.

Aqueles que promovem o conceito de “fortalecimento imune” muitas vezes estão simplesmente tentando obter lucro. A própria ideia de “fortalecimento” pode criar uma sensação de carência — de que a saúde de alguém poderia (sempre) estar melhor. Isso enquadra o estado de saúde como um déficit que exige que as pessoas busquem continuamente esforços de restauração ou otimização — uma estratégia de marketing de saúde e bem-estar comumente utilizada.

O primeiro passo é estabelecer uma lacuna, acompanhada de ansiedade ou medo. O segundo passo é oferecer ações que possam ser adquiridas para preencher essa lacuna.

Nossa pesquisa no Instagram durante a pandemia, por exemplo, constatou que mais de 96% do conteúdo sobre fortalecimento imune que analisamos provinha de criadores que vendiam ou anunciavam produtos ou serviços. Identificamos 62 empresas diferentes marcadas em uma amostra de 28 publicações.

Também refletimos sobre como a própria hashtag das redes sociais #immunebooster funcionava como um produto retórico usado para “gerar atividade na economia da atenção online”.

Outras empresas podem promover produtos ou serviços que supostamente fortalecem o sistema imune com alegações nesse sentido, como hidroterapia, infusões intravenosas, limpezas e desintoxicações. No passado, empresas de cereais também comercializaram seus produtos como “auxiliares” da imunidade. Não há evidências sólidas de que qualquer uma dessas atividades traga benefícios à função imune.

Suplementos alimentares na forma de vitaminas, minerais ou ervas também oferecem benefícios limitados para quem não apresenta deficiências diagnosticadas.

Conforme observado em um artigo sobre fortalecimento imune publicado por uma rede farmacêutica canadense, “ até o momento, nenhum medicamento, produto ou remédio natural foi oficialmente aprovado pelo Ministério da Saúde do Canadá para fortalecer o sistema imune”. Empresas, no entanto, comercializam produtos como fortalecedores explícitos ou, de maneira geral, como produtos que oferecem “benefícios ao sistema imune”.

Uma pesquisa recente de nossa equipe, por exemplo, avaliou a comercialização de suplementos de “células-tronco” no marketplace de comércio eletrônico da Amazon. Descobrimos que mais de 40% dos produtos alegavam benefícios relacionados à imunidade.

Os suplementos são hoje um grande negócio, com uma mercado avaliado na casa das centenas de bilhões de dólares. Não é surpreendente encontrar uma abordagem de marketing ampla e abrangente para produtos como os suplementos de “células-tronco”, que não apresentam evidências claras de eficácia para nenhuma condição de saúde

A comercialização da imunidade é uma preocupação para todos nós. Espaços de saúde comercializados podem prejudicar a confiança nos sistemas de saúde e gerar confusão sobre em quem e no que confiamos.

Se nossas percepções forem moldadas por empresas e influenciadores, isso pode influenciar negativamente atividades essenciais de saúde baseadas em evidências, como a vacinação. A disseminação desenfreada de desinformação sobre vacinas durante a pandemia desestimulou a adesão à vacinação e contribuiu para promover noções incorretas sobre imunidade pessoal.

A relutância em relação à vacina é altamente complexa, com múltiplos fatores em jogo. A política e a polarização são, cada vez mais, forças influentes. O discurso impreciso sobre imunidade apenas obscurece ainda mais o panorama informativo e, por sua vez, a tomada de decisão sobre a vacinação.

O marketing de saúde e bem-estar é astuto e sedutor, cuidadosamente elaborado para despertar nosso interesse e oferecer soluções. No ambiente midiático atual, todos precisamos ser cautelosos e críticos em relação às empresas que comercializam produtos e serviços voltados para nossa saúde e bem-estar. Isso é importante ao avaliar a preparação para qualquer pandemia futura e como nossos sistemas de saúde podem construir e manter a confiança do público.

Uma compreensão precisa da imunidade nos ajuda a manter um sistema imune que funcione bem, e uma sociedade que também funcione bem.

Alessandro Marcon é pesquisador associado sênior no Health Law Institute, Universidade de Alberta. Ele é afiliado ao Bridge Research Consortium (BRC).

Jia Hu é médico(a) de Saúde Pública, Programas de Imunização e Prevenção e Promoção da Saúde da Universidade da Colúmbia Britânica. Ele trabalha no Centro de Controle de Doenças da Colúmbia Britânica, onde sua atuação se concentra em imunizações e doenças evitáveis por vacinação.

articles.title: Estado é condenado após alunos induzirem menino autista a lamber chão | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso aconteceu durante o intervalo em escola estadual de Santos (SP). Justiça fixou indenização de R$ 15 mil ao menino de 11 anos e determinou acompanhamento escolar. Estado ainda pode recorrer.
articles.summary: Caso aconteceu durante o intervalo em escola estadual de Santos. Justiça fixou indenização de R$ 15 mil ao menino de 11 anos. Estado ainda pode recorrer.
articles.body:
Imagem ilustrativa de menino em escola — Foto: Reprodução/Canção Nova

O Estado de São Paulo foi condenado a indenizar em R$ 15 mil um menino de 11 anos , diagnosticado com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA), que foi induzido por alunos mais velhos a lamber o chão da escola onde estudava em Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, em troca de R$ 20.

Além da indenização por danos morais, com acréscimo de juros e correção monetária, a Justiça determinou que o estado disponibilize um profissional de apoio escolar para acompanhar o menino durante todo o período de aulas na unidade onde está matriculado.

Ao g1 , o Estado de São Paulo informou que ainda não foi intimado da decisão da 2ª Vara da Fazenda Pública de Santos. Ainda cabe recurso.

Conforme sentença, obtida pelo g1 nesta segunda-feira (9), o caso aconteceu em 25 de fevereiro de 2025, no pátio da Escola Estadual Professora Alzira Martins Lichti, no Morro Nova Cintra.

Na ação, foram apresentados diagnósticos do estudante de TEA, Retardo Mental Moderado e Transtorno Opositivo-Desafiador.

O menino relatou ter sido vítima de alunos mais velhos durante o intervalo. Segundo ele, foi induzido a lamber o chão em troca de R$ 20, "sob zombarias de outros estudantes e sem intervenção preventiva de funcionários, sofrendo humilhação de grande repercussão".

Ainda de acordo com o relato, a direção da escola orientou a mãe a não levá-lo às aulas até o retorno de uma consulta médica. A situação motivou a transferência do estudante para outra escola estadual.

Caso aconteceu na Escola Estadual Professora Alzira Martins Lichti, no Morro Nova Cintra, em Santos, SP — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Na ação apresentada à Justiça, a defesa do menino apontou falhas da escola na vigilância dos alunos e na oferta de apoio especializado. Também pediu indenização de R$ 100 mil por danos morais, custeio de acompanhamento psicológico e disponibilização de um profissional de apoio escolar.

O juiz Bruno Nascimento Troccoli reconheceu o direito à indenização, mas considerou o pedido de R$ 100 mil desproporcional aos critérios adotados pelo Tribunal de Justiça de São Paulo em casos semelhantes ocorridos no ambiente escolar. O valor foi fixado em R$ 15 mil.

Para definir a quantia, o magistrado afirmou ter considerado "as particularidades do fato, a intensidade da humilhação suportada pelo incapaz em virtude de sua vulnerabilidade cognitiva, o desvio comportamental dos envolvidos, a omissão inicial na comunicação à família e os princípios da razoabilidade e proporcionalidade, evitando o enriquecimento sem causa".

" A interrupção tardia dos atos ofensivos pela coordenadora e a total ausência de comunicação imediata do gravíssimo episódio à genitora do incapaz, que apenas tomou conhecimento da humilhação ao ser alertada pela filha em momento posterior, denotam indiscutível falha de vigilância, prevenção e manejo institucional", disse o juiz, destacando que a situação foi " deprimente e vexatória " .

Troccoli acrescentou que a postura posterior da direção, ao solicitar que o estudante retornasse às aulas apenas depois de uma consulta médica, "agravou a sensação de desamparo e desrespeito aos direitos fundamentais da criança ".

O magistrado também determinou que o estado disponibilize um profissional de apoio escolar ao menino. Na decisão, destacou que um médico neurologista e a própria Secretaria de Educação confirmaram a necessidade de acompanhamento contínuo durante as atividades escolares.

Já sobre o pedido de acompanhamento psicológico, o juiz afirmou que o atendimento é uma providência de saúde já assegurada pela rede pública e que a mãe deverá buscar os canais regulares de atendimento multiprofissional do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

articles.title: 8-year-old Haitian boy placed in federal custody alone after ICE check-in
articles.summary: ICE said the boy's uncle could not establish legal guardianship.
articles.body:
An 8-year-old Haitian boy who lost Temporary Protected Status earlier this year was taken into federal custody after an immigration check-in, according to local advocates and school officials.

The third grader, who attends Fay Elementary School in San Diego, was placed into government custody alone after attending an Immigration and Customs Enforcement appointment with his uncle on Thursday, according to his school district and an advocacy group.

"The eight-year-old received a letter to meet with an ICE agent," the San Diego Unified School District said in a letter to DHS. "His uncle, with whom he's been living since the child's father was deported more than a year ago, took him to meet the agent because he did not want to break the law."

Advocates and school officials said the boy had been living with his uncle and cousins after his father was deported to Mexico last year.

"They did not give the father the opportunity or chance to actually put in place legal guardianship for the kid," said Guerline Jozef, the executive director of the nonprofit Haitian Bridge Alliance.

Cody Petterson, a board trustee with the SDUSD, told ABC News the uncle was designated on school records as an authorized caregiver.

A spokesperson for ICE told ABC News in a statement that because the uncle could not establish legal guardianship, agents treated the 8-year-old as an unaccompanied child under the Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act, a federal law that provides protections for unaccompanied immigrant children.

The agency did not allege any wrongdoing or abuse by the uncle, but invoked the law to mandate the child's transfer after designating him as an unaccompanied minor.

"Out of an abundance of caution and to ensure the child's safety, ICE determined it was best to remove the child from the household and place him in the care of the Office of Refugee Resettlement," the spokesperson said.

According to the school district and an advocacy group, the 8-year-old remains in ORR custody. It is unclear if he will be removed from the U.S.

Jozef called the detention "an excuse for [ICE] to remove the child and potentially put him in deportation proceedings."

"He was dressed very well, and he is very well cared for," Jozef added. "There's absolutely no reason for them to remove him from the care of his relatives without putting in place proper procedures for him, knowing very well that ICE already deported the father."

In the letter to DHS, San Diego Unified School District officials said they have "witnessed situations in which children who should be attending school and participating in a supportive educational environment instead find themselves in government facilities."

"Children should not lose access to education simply because of circumstances unfolding around them," the district said.

articles.title: Trump's $1.5tn defence budget to be blocked by Democrats
articles.summary: Republicans' midterm defeat is crushing any remaining hopes that Congress would approve President Donald Trump's unprecedented $1.5 trillion defence
articles.body: Republicans' midterm defeat is crushing any remaining hopes that Congress would approve President Donald Trump's unprecedented $1.5 trillion defence budget request amid an unpopular war in the Middle East.Democrats, who won solid majorities of both chambers of Congress on Tuesday, were already largely opposed to the 44% increase from the previous fiscal year and are now signalling they will block any efforts to push it forward.At the same time, Republican lawmakers returning to the lame-duck session before the new Congress is seated in Jan may not be able to muster the support or political will to ram through the massive defence spending package, especially amid Pentagon's unpopular war against Iran that cost many of them their jobs."We must push for the development of a more realistic and sustainable approach to our national security - one that does not require a defense budget in excess of $1 trillion or one paid for with draconian cuts to critical domestic programs," Representative Adam Smith of Washington, the incoming chairman of House Armed Services Committee, said in a statement after the election.The Democratic resistance risks imperilling some of Trump's splashiest defence ambitions, including Golden Dome missile shield and his Trump-class battleship plan, and bodes poorly for defence contractors - some of which also face the prospect of congressional scrutiny over alleged conflicts of interest with the Trump administration.Shares of major contractors, including Lockheed Martin and Northrop Grumman, fell this week as the midterm results eroded expectations of a ramp-up in US military spending.Trump on Sunday said he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progress, CNN reported. "It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," CNN cited Trump as saying in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."Meanwhile, the US military has announced it will create a 20-member task force to find ways to disrupt land routes into Iran that it says are used for shipments of weapons and illicit materials. articles.summary: CHHATARPUR: At least 35 people, including children, suffered burn injuries in separate firecracker-related incidents during Diwali celebrations on Sunday
articles.body: CHHATARPUR: At least 35 people, including children, suffered burn injuries in separate firecracker-related incidents during Diwali celebrations on Sunday and were admitted to the district hospital in Madhya Pradesh’s Chhatarpur.Dr Rajesh Mishra told news agency ANI, "During the Diwali festival, we have received a significant number of cases involving burns from gunpowder and firecrackers. The patients include individuals of various ages, from children to the elderly, and all are currently undergoing treatment.""Some patients have been discharged after initial first aid was administered. These incidents often stemmed from a lack of caution, either by the children themselves or their parents, while bursting firecrackers. So far, we have received approximately 35 to 40 patients, " Mishra added.On November 5, Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav virtually held a meeting with Collectors and Superintendents of Police (SPs) at CM House, directing officials to ensure foolproof law and order arrangements for peaceful Diwali celebrations.CM Yadav also directed officials to strictly prevent the use of banned firecrackers, carbide guns and carbide lamps, citing their harmful effects on human health.He urged people to celebrate Diwali with joy and enthusiasm while ensuring that no unlawful or anti-social activities take place. He also asked the administration to remain on high alert throughout the festive period. articles.title: Gujarati-origin man indicted in US over $2m Ponzi scheme
articles.summary: AHMEDABAD: A Gujarati-origin man who allegedly duped investors in the US through a Ponzi scheme involving nearly $2 million has been indicted by a federal
articles.body: AHMEDABAD: A Gujarati-origin man who allegedly duped investors in the US through a Ponzi scheme involving nearly $2 million has been indicted by a federal grand jury in New Hampshire on charges of wire fraud.This marks a fresh development in a case that had earlier drawn the attention of state securities regulators in the US.Kevin Patel, who founded and operated Royal Investments LLC, allegedly solicited investments from people across the US by promising to invest their money in the stock market and guarantee annual returns of 12% to 16%, according to an indictment filed in the US district court for New Hampshire on Nov 4.The indictment alleges that Patel founded the company in 2018 and marketed it as "The Company of Wealth & Trust".Investors were promised quarterly interest payments and a full return of their principal at the end of fixed investment terms, with assurances that they would suffer no losses.However, prosecutors allege that Royal Investments was a Ponzi scheme in which almost none of the investors' funds were actually invested.Instead, the money was allegedly diverted towards personal expenses, payments to family members and repayment of earlier investors using funds collected from new investors.The alleged scheme operated from at least Feb 2020 until April 2026. Patel allegedly ran out of funds towards the end of 2024 and stopped making interest and principal payments, leaving investors with losses running into several hundred thousand dollars.The indictment cites three wire transfers - $50,000 from New Jersey in March 2023 and two transfers of $50,000 and $30,000 from Florida in Nov and Dec 2023 - as specific instances of the alleged fraud.The latest federal action follows proceedings initiated by New Hampshire securities regulators in Dec 2025.The state had accused Patel and Royal Investments of operating without the required licences and allegedly defrauding four investors of nearly $386,000. Regulators had sought restitution, penalties and a permanent ban on securities-related activities.The federal indictment charges Patel with three counts of wire fraud. articles.title: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport, identity card to facilitate return to Bangladesh
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would beannounced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.Death sentence and legal proceedingsIn November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Political implications of her returnHasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Seattle redesigned Stone Way with two traffic lanes, a center turn lane and bike facilities; total crashes fell 14%, injury crashes 33% and pedestrian crashes 80%
articles.summary: The redesign of Seattle's Stone Way reduced crashes by 14%, injuries by 33%, and pedestrian collisions by 80%, highlighting the effectiveness of road diets in promoting safety and encouraging cycling.
articles.body: In July 2007, Seattle repaved part of Stone Way North, a four-lane street linking Fremont and Wallingford neighbourhoods. The city used the repaving to restripe it with two travel lanes, a centre turn lane, bike lanes and sharrows. Local business owners pushed back because they saw Stone Way as a vital arterial, a detail recorded in the road diet case study from the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA). The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) evaluated the results in a May 2010 report, Stone Way N Rechannelization: Before and After Study. Total collisions fell 14%, injury collisions 33% and pedestrian collisions 80%. The numbers behind those percentages are smaller than they sound.Seattle restriped Stone Way in two phasesSDOT’s study area ran approximately 1.2 miles, from N 34th Street to N 50th Street, on a street that carried about 13,000 vehicles a day. As mentioned in the above study, N 40th Street to N 50th Street was restriped in August 2007, while N 34th Street to N 40th Street followed in April 2008. The report provides a number of reasons that led to this change. There were new crosswalk standards in 2004, so existing crosswalks would need to be striped out.Collisions fell from 159 to 137 across matching 28-month periodsIn the report’s comparison of April 5, 2005 to August 6, 2007 with August 7, 2007 to December 4, 2009, total collisions fell from 159 to 137 and injury collisions from 52 to 35. Pedestrian crashes decreased from 5 to 1, making the 80% decrease four crashes. Angle collisions fell 56%, and the share of collisions involving an injury dropped from 33% to 25%. Bicycle crashes were still seven in both time periods, but with an increase in bicycle trips, the number of crashes per bicycle trip had decreased.One type of collision went the wrong way. Rear-end collisions rose 65%, from 17 to 28, mostly between N 39th and N 41st Streets, where the road shifted from four lanes to three during the interim period between August 2007 and April 2008, when only part of the corridor had been restriped. The same report states that the driver had trouble making left turns at the location and acknowledged the two-year period to be difficult to quantify statically.Top-end speeding dropped by about 75%The posted speed limit was 30 mph. Before the change, the report put the 85th percentile speed at approximately 37 mph and it dropped by about 1 mph northbound and 3 mph southbound. Those driving at 10 mph or more over the posted speed limit decreased by about 75%. Traffic in excess of 40 mph reduced from about 4% or 150 vehicles per day to 1%, or less than 25 vehicles per day. The speed drop matters for pedestrians, since the United Kingdom study Killing Speed and Saving Lives, cited in the report, put a pedestrian’s chance of surviving a hit at 85% at 20 mph and 15% at 40 mph.Throughput was maintained and cycling increasedThere was a reduction in average daily traffic of vehicles by about 6%, whereas there was an increase in the number of bicycles by 35% between 2007 and 2010. In SDOT’s counts, daily traffic on parallel streets fell 12% to 34%, which suggests drivers did not divert onto side streets. At N 42nd Street, peak hour volume has been reduced by less than 5% and at N 48th Street by 13%.Other road diets show a similar rangeA November 2014 FHWA newsletter, Using Road Diets to Advance Healthy, Safe Communities, put the crash rate reduction from road diets at 19% to 47%. The newsletter’s other example, East Boulevard in Charlotte, North Carolina, is a 35 mph street where the 85th percentile speed dropped from 43 mph to 40 mph and crashes on one segment fell from 2.64 to 1.67 per month. On the other segment of East Boulevard, the drop was smaller, from 1.97 to 1.86 crashes per month. It should be noted from the newsletter that road diets are not suitable for all roads and that streets with less than 20,000 vehicles per day may be considered for further study.You use AI every day. articles.title: Turkiye pushes electrification top of climate agenda as COP31 set to open
articles.summary: Ankara aims to make electricity account for 35 percent of global energy demand by 2035.
articles.body:
The United Nations climate conference COP31 is set to open on Monday in Antalya, Turkiye, against the backdrop of the US-led war on Iran, which has underscored the world’s attachment to fossil fuels.

Turkiye has said it would centre electrification on the COP31 agenda, launching the non-binding 35-by-35 Global Electrification Pledge, which aims to make electricity account for at least 35 percent of global energy demand by 2035.

Electricity currently accounts for about one-fifth of global total final energy consumption, according to the International Energy Agency.

Turkiye says the “35 by 35” will speed up the shift to renewable sources of energy while strengthening energy security.

“This year’s energy crisis has shocked us… everyone now understands that energy that you import is energy that you do not control,” the COP31 president and Turkiye’s environment minister, Murat Kurum, said on Thursday.

“Electrification is the answer. It protects communities from volatile global markets and cuts emissions.”

COP31’s aim is “to usher in the age of electricity”, he said.

The climate conference’s priority areas also include zero waste, methane reduction, climate-resilient cities, green industrialisation, education and implementation of national climate plans.

However, climate advocates have criticised the pledge, arguing it does not require that additional electricity come from low-carbon sources.

This has set up a debate on whether electrification alone should count as climate progress.

A coalition of countries, including South Pacific island nations most vulnerable to sea level rise, is pushing more generally for a clearer global roadmap away from fossil fuels.

Many oil and gas producing countries, including Saudi Arabia, argue that fossil fuels can form a substantial part of the global energy mix, provided they are paired with technologies that reduce or capture emissions.

The US-Israel war on Iran has severely disrupted oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, raising fuel prices around the globe and leading governments to scramble for alternative sources.

US President Donald Trump has encouraged policies maximising oil, gas, and coal production to address the Middle East disruptions.

South Korea, India, Thailand and other Asian nations have increased their reliance on coal or taken steps to boost coal-fired power generation.

At the same time, the deployment of renewable energy has also risen, driven by surging exports of cheap clean technology from China.

articles.title: After knife-edge vote, New Zealand parties put off coalitions talks
articles.summary: New Zealand has just seen its tightest general election in years, with the two major parties neck-and-neck.
articles.body:
Who will form New Zealand's next government remains uncertain after the country's national election on Saturday, with final results not due for another couple of weeks.

It's the tightest vote that the country has seen in years, with the incumbent National Party and opposition Labour Party neck-and-neck in terms of party vote share.

In terms of seats, a National-led conservative coalition, which includes the Act Party and NZ First, are projected to win a combined 67 seats - giving them a narrow one-seat majority.

As questions about other coalitions swirl, party leaders are remaining tight-lipped, saying they would wait for the final results before formal discussions.

Major parties on both sides of the political aisle were "likely dissatisfied with their campaigns", Max Rashbrooke, adjunct senior research fellow at the Victoria University of Wellington, told the BBC.

The opposition Labour Party, led by Chris Hipkins, ran an election campaign that "seems to have inspired few voters", despite going up against Christopher Luxon, a "historically unpopular prime minister", Rashbrooke said.

On the other hand, he added, the incumbent National Party also "failed to spark enthusiasm" even though it "should have been safe" given the country hasn't seen a one-term government in more than 50 years.

The election dealt a huge blow to National with the loss of some of its most senior lawmakers, including Finance Minister Nicola Willis, Justice Minister Paul Goldsmith, Transport Minister Chris Bishop and House Speaker Gerry Brownlee.

Act Party leader David Seymour has expressed interest in the finance minister portfolio, telling news outlet Stuff that National must recognise the voters' message and let its coalition partners play a bigger role.

"The government barely survived, it must now put its best foot forward in every step," he said.

The big winners of election night were "the more radical minor parties", Rashbrooke said.

The left-leaning Greens and the right-wing libertarian Act Party both saw new highs this election, while the Opportunity Party, a fledgling centrist party, scored a breakout victory. Having previously failed three times at getting into Parliament, it's now projected to get seven seats.

Opportunity's incoming lawmakers, including leader Qiulae Wong, arrived at New Zealand's parliament on Monday morning, for the start of what Wong said would be a week of "induction stuff".

Opportunity, which has rejected traditional political divisions, has said it's open to forming a coalition with either major party.

Whichever coalition they join, though, they would "really need to be comfortable with the overall direction the government is going in", Wong told reporters on Monday.

Wong said that although she has received calls of congratulations from Labour's Hipkins and the Greens' Chlöe Swarbrick, they have not had any discussions about coalitions.

Luxon, who had previously ruled out working with Opportunity, told public broadcaster RNZ on Monday that he wanted to talk to Wong "shortly".

Counting is still underway for nearly 400,000 "special votes", which includes those from overseas voters and people outside of their electorate.

These make up 14% of total votes, and are likely to be important in the final count.

"They tend to lean left, as voters casting special votes tend to be younger and more likely to be renters - and therefore more likely to be living outside their electorate," senior politics lecturer Claire Timperley told the BBC on election night.

"The overseas vote might be more likely than usual to be disaffected by the current coalition, given we've seen increasing numbers of New Zealanders moving overseas as a result of cost-of-living challenges."

Faced with a stagnating economy and challenging job market, a record number of Kiwis are moving overseas in search of better career opportunities. More than 114,000 people migrated out of the country in the year leading up to August.

Young people the BBC spoke to ahead of the election said they were "tired" and "cynical" about the future - part of what polling shows is a general grim mood across the country.

"In New Zealand as elsewhere, politics is splintering. But which parties ultimately benefit remains unclear for now," said Rashbrooke.

Final election results are expected on 27 November, with the official confirmation of MPs set for 3 December.

articles.title: ‘Tents don’t protect us’: Rains flood displaced Palestinians in Gaza
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of Palestinians are vulnerable to flooding as Israel continues to block entry of mobile homes.
articles.body:
Az-Zawayda, Gaza Strip – On Saturday night, water began rushing into Jaber al-Kaseeh’s tent in central Gaza’s az-Zawayda area, waking him and his family as heavy rain swept across Gaza. Soon the tent’s floor was flooded, soaking mattresses, carpets, blankets and spoiling what little food the family had managed to keep.

“Everyone woke up and stayed awake, asking their neighbours about the extent of damage and inquiring about children,” Jaber, who is in his 70s, told Al Jazeera.

He described the area outside the displacement camp, where thousands of Palestinians have taken refuge, as a swimming pool.

More than 70,000 tents have been flooded since heavy rains began late on Friday, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office. Hundreds of thousands of displaced Palestinians are sheltering in locations considered “highly vulnerable” to more flooding.

More than a year after the so-called “ceasefire” deal was signed between Israel and Hamas, Israel has continued to flout the terms of the agreement, blocking the entry of goods into Gaza, including 60,000 mobile homes and 200,000 tents.

Only 20,000 tents have been allowed in, and mobile homes have remained parked on the Egyptian side of the border, many of them for more than two years.

This is the fourth winter for Jaber and his family living in a tent house in the az-Zawayda area. Originally from Beit Lahiya in northern Gaza, Jaber has been displaced several times, like most Palestinians since Israel launched its genocidal war on October 7, 2023.

More than 90 percent of Palestinians have been displaced, many of them multiple times, by the war that has attracted global condemnation.

Jaber says his camp was flooded three or four times last winter, forcing many families to leave. Around 40 tents still remain there, but the latest flooding has left them in even worse condition.

“All the tents are now damaged, torn and covered in mud,” Jaber told Al Jazeera.

“We urgently need tents, tarpaulins, plastic sheets, mattresses, blankets and carpets to protect us from the difficult days ahead.

“We keep hearing about tents and tarpaulins being distributed, but we have received nothing.

“We had hoped the mobile homes and temporary housing units promised under the ceasefire deal would allow us to rest and return to a life of safety and peace. But it was all just words in the air. We have seen nothing.”

Jaber’s experience reflects the wider shelter crisis facing displaced Palestinians across Gaza. Despite the “ceasefire” agreement, which included provisions for temporary housing units, tents and heavy machinery to clear rubble, large numbers of families remain in makeshift shelters exposed to winter weather.

Under the first phase of the agreement, along with temporary housing units and tents, heavy equipment was also supposed to be allowed in to remove rubble and help restore damaged infrastructure.

But the arrival of mobile homes and heavy machinery has been delayed as Israel has found excuses to restrict their entry into the enclave of 2.3 million people.

Trucks carrying mobile homes and equipment have reportedly been waiting on the Egyptian side of the border while Palestinians live in misery in dilapidated tent camps.

According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), Gaza requires approximately 121,000 tents and 561,000 tarpaulins, while available stocks remain far below what is needed.

For Om Hani Hamouda, a displaced woman from Beit Lahiya now sheltering in al-Zawayda, replacing her worn-out tent with a caravan has become a dream.

“We did not expect that the first rainfall would leave us in this condition,” she told Al Jazeera. “These tents do not protect us from the cold, storms or rain. Whenever winter comes, everyone holds their breath.”

Hamouda had hoped the ceasefire agreement would allow her family to return to northern Gaza or at least receive a caravan or building materials to secure better shelter. But she said there had been no sign of progress.

“We are asking for a dignified life. We want these tents to be replaced with caravans. Even a simple caravan would be better,” she told Al Jazeera.

Hamouda’s family has been displaced around 15 times during the war. She spent more than 15 years living and working in the United Arab Emirates before returning to Gaza nearly two years before the war began.

“My children cry because they miss the life we had there,” she said. “Life here is so difficult. There is no life in any sense.”

Ramy Abdu, chairman of the Euro-Mediterranean Human Rights Monitor, told Al Jazeera that large quantities of tents, caravans, prefabricated housing units and shelter equipment remain stranded at Gaza’s borders because of Israeli restrictions.

He said that while more than 1.5 million displaced Palestinians were facing another winter in worn-out tents, even people living in houses and apartments remained exposed to the elements because of the extensive damage to homes and infrastructure.

“Today, we cannot even say that those living in houses and apartments are safe from extreme weather because, with around 85 percent of homes destroyed or damaged, every family is exposed to some degree of harsh weather conditions,” Abdu said, adding that Israel continues to reject shipments containing timber and emergency shelter kits, depriving families of the ability to repair homes that could otherwise accommodate them.

Abdu said Israel, as the occupying power, was legally obligated under the Fourth Geneva Convention to ensure essential supplies reached civilians and to facilitate humanitarian relief.

Jihad Dawwas, 51, says he felt helpless as he could not do anything as his children had nowhere dry to sleep amid the rains.

Water poured into the tents at the displacement camp where he is sheltering, while strong winds blew away many of the surrounding tents. His children ended up sleeping while standing, he said, after rainwater soaked their mattresses and the plastic sheets covering their shelter.

“They slept standing up. By morning, some of my children had become ill because of the cold and the storm,” he told Al Jazeera.

Dawwas, who was displaced from northern Gaza, is sheltering with seven of his own children and three orphaned children of his brother. He said he had bought the family’s tent with his own money and had received no tent from any charity or aid initiative.

“A tent cannot replace a home, not even by one percent,” he said. “We are living in what is left of our lives.”

He said he had seen no caravans or temporary housing units arrive to help displaced families, despite the expectations raised by the ceasefire agreement.

“Our lives are a daily hell. We are completely forgotten. There is no fair distribution of aid, and no one is really asking about us,” Dawwas said.

He questioned why even basic shelter supplies had become so difficult to obtain.

“Do tents and tarpaulins really need all this pressure and effort just to become something we can ask for?” he asked. “They should provide us with tents and tarpaulins, and give us at least a dignified life.”

articles.title: Smog blankets New Delhi as Diwali firecrackers worsen air quality
articles.summary: Air quality in Indian capital reaches severe levels, posing heightened health risks for more than 30 million residents.
articles.body:
Heavy smog has blanketed New Delhi after firecrackers lit up the Indian capital during Diwali celebrations , worsening the seasonal pollution crisis.

Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights, was celebrated across India on Sunday. Despite restrictions on fireworks, New Delhi residents celebrated the festival of lights with firecrackers throughout Sunday evening, releasing smoke and fine particulate matter into the atmosphere.

On Monday morning, the Air Quality Index exceeded 350 in several parts of the capital, categorised as “severe” and posing significant health risks, according to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recommended exposure thresholds.

Last month, India’s Supreme Court put in place restrictions to limit Diwali pollution, allowing only approved “green firecrackers” under specified conditions for three-hour windows on Saturday and Sunday. The approved crackers produce fewer emissions but are not pollution-free.

On Wednesday, days before Diwali, toxic air pollution in New Delhi surged to more than 30 times the WHO’s recommended daily limit, data from air monitors showed.

New Delhi, home to 30 million people, persistently ranks among the world’s most polluted capital cities.

The issue is exacerbated during the winter, when cooler temperatures, low wind speeds and stagnant atmospheric conditions prevent pollutants from dispersing.

Vehicles account for 23 percent of New Delhi’s winter pollution, while biomass burning, including farm stubble fires, contributes 20 percent, according to India’s Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

The result is a thick haze that can linger over the capital and surrounding areas for days.

articles.title: Charity wants Thames Valley bee, bird and butterfly population boost
articles.summary: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust aims to raise £70,000 for the project.
articles.body:
A charity wants to raise £70,000 for a project aimed at boosting wildlife populations on farmland in the Thames Valley.

The Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust (BBOWT) said the money would form part of its Nature Recovery Fund and would be used to tackle falling numbers of birds, bees and butterflies.

The trust said farmland bird populations had fallen by 63% since 1970, while half of the UK's 27 bumblebee species were in decline.

It said measures to help wildlife could include using fewer chemicals in farming to create healthier soil and less polluted waterways, as well as setting aside corners of grassland for animals.

BBOWT's chief executive Estelle Bailey said: "Farmland makes up 68% of our three counties, so to truly have an impact on nature's recovery, our work must expand far beyond our precious nature reserves."

In 2023, a report produced by government agencies, environmental groups and universities found one in six species in the UK were at risk of extinction.

Bailey added: "I want future generations to experience the joy of countryside filled with life - swallows darting above fields, butterflies and bumblebees feeding on abundant wildflowers, hedgerows alive with the sound of birdsong, and to eat locally grown food that supports a healthy, resilient landscape."

articles.title: Photos reveal The Smiths' 'dramatic' Manchester farewell
articles.summary: Rarely-seen images from what proved to be the iconic band's penultimate show surface 40 years on.
articles.body:
Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments.

And it was where The Smiths, one of Manchester's most iconic bands, played what would prove to be their final farewell to the city on 30 October 1986.

Forty years on, rarely-seen photos of the show, taken by then-student Alison Bell show what she said was a "dramatic" and "amazing" night.

Bell, who had been drawn to Manchester by its music scene as a student and went on to have a successful career in music promotion, said she had been desperate to see the band and the Free Trade Hall show was "the first opportunity I had to see them".

Formed by singer Morrissey and guitarist Johnny Marr in 1982, the band were at the peak of their powers at the show, riding high on the success of their third long-player, The Queen Is Dead, which would go on to become widely-regarded as one of the greatest albums of all time.

Bell was at the show as a writer for Manchester Polytechnic's student newspaper, Pulp.

"I got given a ticket for it if I would review it and take photographs," she said.

Her role granted her more freedom than the rest of the crowd, as she was able to roam a photographers' area in front of the stage.

"We could just walk from side to side and take pictures," she said.

"Using film... there was no going back, you just took a picture and hoped for the best."

"Obviously, I'd wanted to see them for a long time, so I was just so excited to be there."

She said the gig was "dramatic", with the band entering to Prokofiev's Dance of the Knights.

"They came on stage [and] sang Ask [as] the first song and it was just fantastic."

The set list reads like a greatest hits, with songs from The Queen Is Dead, such as How Soon Is Now? and There Is A Light That Never Goes Out, interspersed with future classics That Joke Isn't Funny Anymore, Panic and Still Ill.

Bell said she also remembered Morrissey waving placards bearing the words The Queen Is Dead and Two Light Ales, Please.

The latter phrase would become part of Smiths folklore and inspired the name of a fanzine about the band.

Bell said she took more than 30 photos on the night, but only one was used by the student newspaper.

That left her with an archive of images of a gig which unexpectedly gained extra significance after it happened.

The band would only play live once more, at a charity benefit in London, before the increasingly-strained relationship between Morrissey and Marr boiled over and the guitarist left the band in mid-1987.

"People didn't know they were going to split up, of course," she said

She said she put the photos away for safe-keeping, but always had plans to share them when the time was right.

"I'd been meaning to do something with them for a long time and just never got around to it," she said.

She said it was her involvement in fundraising events at Salford Lads Club that caused her to revisit the collection.

The club has been an essential destination for fans after the band used it as the backdrop for a famous photo which featured on the inner sleeve of The Queen Is Dead.

Bell has since worked with designer Martin Holland to produce merchandise, including a T-shirt featuring one of her close-up photographs of Morrissey, with a reproduction of her original concert ticket on the back.

"I had it tucked away... for 40 years," she said.

"I just thought, 'yeah, it is a good photograph and I should let people see it'."

She said she was also considering producing posters and making more of the collection available, but had yet to decide on further plans.

And tantalisingly, she said there may even be more unseen photos, as she believes she has negatives that she did not develop at the time, but has not yet found them.

Fans will hope they turn up and offer a further glimpse into the final moments of an iconic band.
